newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican goes from death row to soap stardom.
newsitem.headline: Mexican goes from death row to soap stardom.

text.p: Mexican immigrant Ricardo Aldape's reprieve from U.S. death row in April had many of the hallmarks of a larger-than-life soap opera. Now he has agreed to go through it again -- this time as a television star.

Aldape, who spent 14 years on death row in Texas before being freed on April 16, has signed with Mexico's Television Azteca to play the part of a hapless immigrant in the broadcaster's latest prime-time hit, To the North of Where the Heart Lies.
Family members said on Wednesday he would star in 15 episodes of the programme, which depicts the troubles which beset Mexicans who illegally cross into the United States.

Few are better qualified to pass on a message. In 1982, Aldape sold his bike, left a brief note for his parents at his home in the northern city of Monterrey, and slipped across the border into Texas in search of a job, money and better prospects.
Two months later he was jailed on charges of shooting to death a Texas policeman. After conviction he sent 14 years on death row, on two occasions coming just hours from lethal injection.

He was freed after a judge threw out tainted testimony and prosecutors decided there was no case against him. Upon release, U.S. Border Patrol agents hauled him to the border in handcuffs and packed him off to Mexico. Here, he was greeted back home like a national hero.

"The money doesn't interest me. What I really want is to leave a message to all those who watch the soap opera. I hope it will mean something that they see what happened to me in flesh and blood," Aldape told El Norte newspaper on Wednesday.
He declined to put a figure on how much he would be paid.
"It is not enough to make me rich, but it won't leave me poor either," he admitted.
